title: Reduce Completed pending proof rows export
summary: Removed the transitional Completed pending-proof rows flat export while preserving mediaPipelineCompletedView.completedPendingProofRows(). Pending Publish confidence and Command History final-placement proof consumers now use the Completed namespace helper, the Completed/Pending browser smoke guards against flat-assignment regression, and generated WebView inventory/contract artifacts report 502 flat exports.
reason: Continue namespace-first WebView cleanup in the touched Completed/Pending proof domain without changing backend ownership, media policy, pending-publish drain, or filesystem mutation behavior.
behavior_before: completedView.js exposed completedPendingProofRows through mediaPipelineCompletedView and as a transitional window.completedPendingProofRows flat export. Pending Publish confidence and Command History final-placement proof helpers still read the flat alias.
behavior_after: completedPendingProofRows remains available through mediaPipelineCompletedView only. The touched consumers use the namespace helper, the Completed/Pending browser smoke fails if the served flat assignment returns, and the documented flat-export count is 502 across 49 files.
tests_added: Extended tests/webview/test_webview_browser_completed_pending_proof_smoke.py to reject a served window.completedPendingProofRows flat assignment.
manual_validation: rg -n "window\\.completedPendingProofRows\\b" apps tests Docs --glob '!Docs/generated/summaries/**' (exit 1, no matches)
rollback_plan: Restore the window.completedPendingProofRows assignment in completedView.js, move the touched consumers back to the flat alias only if compatibility is intentionally required, regenerate the WebView public contract baseline and summaries, and rerun the same WebView/static validation ladder.
notes:
Source-media safety: this is a frontend compatibility-export cleanup only. It does not change backend routes, strict confirmations, repair/apply behavior, pending-publish manifests, drain behavior, filesystem mutation, source/scratch/output handling, FFmpeg arguments, or media policy. No downloads or real-media validation are required for this low-risk WebView namespace cleanup.
